inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement 'Stock-based compensation expense' ($1,592M, ABNB_Annual_FY2025.txt:2116) plus 'taxes paid related to net share settlement of equity awards' ($561M, :2316). Airbnb's adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation publishes no combined equity-award figure, so the two lines are summed per the fallback rule. 9M-2026 run-rate: SBC $1,359M + award taxes $534M = 17.0% of revenue, identical to 9M-2025 (17.0%), i.e. no decline yet.
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares for Q3 2026 (597M, 10-Q EPS note; basic shares outstanding 589M at 30 Sep 2026 = 426M Class A + 163M Class B). 9.6M market-condition RSUs are excluded from the diluted count by the filer. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in owner FCF (charging both would double-count). The flat count is funded: $2,851M repurchased in 9M-2026 (TTM ~$3.9B), $2.7B authorization remaining at 30 Sep 2026.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-18T21:00:00Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 110.81-197.87
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.0% base WACC for a large-cap USD-denominated, net-cash tech marketplace with investment-grade credit rating (senior notes issued Q1-2026 at 4.40%-5.25%); reflects ~4.2% risk-free (10yr UST, 2026) + ~4.8% levered equity-risk premium appropriate for a still-double-digit-growth consumer platform with regulatory/cyclical exposure. Bull -1pp (8.0%) for lower-risk execution on established growth drivers; bear +2pp (11.0%) for regulatory/competitive/macro risk stacking, consistent with charging cyclical/execution risk once (in the scenario driver paths) rather than in WACC alone, though a modest scenario-WACC spread is retained here given the binary regulatory-ban risk profile (NYC precedent) that is not fully captured by growth/margin paths alone.
inputs.lease_treatment: not material -- small office footprint; no separate lease adjustment applied.
inputs.nci_treatment: none — wholly owned, no minority interests.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, scenario-weighted, component route (SKILL.md routing: consumer-internet/marketplace operating company). UPDATE of the 2026-09-25 build for the Q3 2026 10-Q. 10-year horizon retained (owner-FCF margin still ramping). ANCHOR CORRECTIONS now that 10-K/10-Q text is extracted (the prior build had none and estimated): (1) interest income is $705M in FY2025 (10-K :2258), not the $200M estimate, so FY2025 owner FCF is $1,755M (4,646 OCF - 33 capex - 2,153 SBC incl. award taxes - 705 interest), not $2,275M -- memo only on this route, because forward flows are built from adjusted EBITDA, which already excludes interest; (2) net cash now includes short-term investments ($5,318M) alongside cash ($7,272M), the '$12.6B' liquidity the 10-Q cites, against $2,500M senior-note principal (book $2,371M) -- the prior build counted cash only; funds held on behalf of customers ($7,420M) are excluded as they are not shareholders'; (3) D&A is 0.5-0.7% of revenue and FY2025 capex $33M, replacing estimates. KNOWN CONSERVATISM: interest income is earned partly on customer funds (float); that portion (roughly $250-300M/yr pre-tax, rate-sensitive, not separately disclosed) is excluded from the flows and has no matching asset in the bridge, so it is left out of value entirely -- worth very roughly $5-7/share if capitalised. Working capital: Reserve Now, Pay Later has reversed the unearned-fees tailwind (9M-2026 -$209M vs +$198M; unearned fees $1,536M vs $1,820M a year earlier), and total operating working capital was already negative in FY2024 (-$67M) and FY2025 (-$106M); wc_capture is therefore cut to 0 (base/bear) and the FY2026 unwind is charged once in equity_bridge. Qualitative file predates the Q3 call: Q4/FY2027 guidance was not available to this build; year-1 drivers are derived from 9M actuals. Price is a regular-session close.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend of revenue_3yr_cagr (13.4%) and equity_3yr_cagr (13.8%); used as the anchor for base-case Year-1 growth before decelerating toward a ~4.5% terminal rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR is 1.4% (FY2022 $1,682M -> FY2025 $1,755M) against revenue 13.4% and equity 13.8% -- a >30% divergence. Reported FCF grew 10.7%/yr over the same span; the gap is SBC-incl-award-taxes rising from 18.3% to 17.6% of revenue in dollar terms $1,537M -> $2,153M, and interest income rising from $186M to $705M (stripped). On a strict owner basis three years of 13% revenue growth produced almost no growth in cash to owners; the forward build therefore depends on adjusted-EBITDA margin expansion and an SBC glide that has not yet started (9M-2026 SBC-incl-taxes 17.0% of revenue, flat on 9M-2025).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes - interest income), filing-sourced: FY2022 1,682 (3,405-930-607-186); FY2023 772 (3,837-1,120-1,224-721); FY2024 1,629 (4,484-1,407-630-818); FY2025 1,755 (4,613-1,592-561-705). FY2020/21 are negative or IPO-distorted, so no 5yr FCF CAGR. Equity 5yr CAGR (23.1%, from $2,901M at FY2020) is IPO-proceeds-distorted and not used.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue growth 17% (9M-2026 actual +17.9%, Q3 +18.9% and above the $4.69-4.77B guide; assumes Q4 at ~+14-15%), then the prior deceleration path unchanged toward 4.5%. Adjusted EBITDA margin 36.2% in FY2026 (9M-2026 38.4% vs 37.1%; Q4 is seasonally ~28-30%), above the 'at least 35.5%' guide, rejoining the prior path to a 38% mature level. SBC-incl-award-taxes starts at 17.5% (the 9M ratio has not fallen year on year) and glides 1pp/yr to the same 10% terminal level as before -- the glide starts a year later than the prior build assumed. Cash tax path unchanged (FY2025 cash taxes $232M = 11% of owner EBIT; deferred tax assets still $1.8B). Working-capital capture 0: RNPL has removed the pay-at-booking tailwind and total working capital has been a small outflow for three years. D&A 0.5% and capex 0.3% of revenue (0.9% in FY2026 for the New York property purchase) from the filings.

bull.narrative: First-time booker growth keeps accelerating (11% YoY in Q2 2026, a 4-year high), Services and Experiences scale into a meaningful new GBV pool beyond Stays, and the 2027 AI travel agent becomes a genuine demand-generation and conversion advantage rather than a defensive move -- letting Airbnb win the AI-interface layer instead of being disintermediated by it. EBITDA margin expands further (toward a Booking-Holdings-like ~41%) as AI compresses concept-to-launch time and support cost structurally, and regulatory bans stay pocketed (NYC-style) rather than spreading to Airbnb's largest markets. UPDATE 2026-11-19: FY2026 growth 18.5% (needs Q4 at ~+20%), margin 36.6%, SBC starting 17.3% and reaching the same 8% terminal level; working-capital capture cut 15% -> 5% (RNPL).

bear.narrative: Regulatory bans (the NYC precedent) spread to more major-metro markets, structurally shrinking addressable host supply; Booking.com and hotel loyalty programs keep taking share as they push further into alternative accommodations, compressing take rate; Services/Experiences investment ($200M+/yr) fails to scale into a durable new revenue line and stays a margin drag rather than a diversification win; and travel spending softens in a discretionary-spending downturn, consistent with the September 2026 sector-wide selloff (ABNB -10%+ over two sessions on sentiment alone). AI travel agents from OpenAI/Google-class entrants intermediate a growing share of trip planning before Airbnb's own 2027 agent ships, eroding the direct demand-side relationship the network-effect moat depends on. UPDATE 2026-11-19: with nine months reported, FY2026 cannot be the bear year -- growth 16% (Q4 at ~+9%) and margin 36.0%; the compression path is unchanged but starts from the higher FY2026 level and reaches the same 32% floor by year 4. Working-capital capture 0.

scenario_narratives.base: Growth lands at ~17% in FY2026 on a strong Q3 (revenue +19%, GBV +21%), then decelerates on the prior path to ~4.5%; EBITDA margin expands from ~36% to 38%; SBC glides from a still-heavy 17.5% of revenue to 10%, a decline that has not yet begun in the reported numbers; no working-capital tailwind now that Reserve Now, Pay Later defers fee collection.
scenario_narratives.bull: First-time-booker acceleration, successful Services/Experiences scaling, and a 2027 AI agent that wins rather than loses the AI-interface layer combine to sustain higher growth and push margins toward Booking-Holdings-like maturity (~41% EBITDA).
scenario_narratives.bear: Regulatory bans spread beyond NYC, Booking.com/hotel-loyalty competition compresses take rate, Services/Experiences investment fails to pay back, and third-party AI agents disintermediate direct bookings ahead of Airbnb's own 2027 launch, all against a discretionary-travel-spending downturn.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 retained, unchanged from the prior build. Bear at 15%: no refinancing or solvency risk (investment-grade, $10.1B net cash, fixed-rate notes to 2036) -- the bear is growth/margin compression, not going-concern. Base 50%. Bull held at 35% rather than raised despite the Q3 beat, because it still needs several independent things to work (Services/Experiences product-market fit, winning the AI interface layer, share gains against Booking).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Airbnb is a high-margin, asset-light marketplace with $10.1B of net cash and a durable network-effect moat, but on a strict owner basis (SBC and award taxes expensed, interest income stripped) FY2025 owner FCF was $1.76B, barely above FY2022. The house-basis weighted value sits below the current price after the post-Q2/Q3 rally; the price sits inside the house-street band, i.e. the market is giving partial credit for treating stock compensation as non-cash. The valuation rests on EBITDA-margin expansion and an SBC glide that the reported numbers have not yet started to show. Float income on customer funds is deliberately left out of value (a conservatism of roughly $5-7/share).
key_risks_to_valuation: SBC glide: 17.5% -> 10% of revenue is assumed, while 9M-2026 shows no decline; each 1pp of terminal SBC is worth several dollars per share
Regulatory bans/restrictions on short-term rentals spreading beyond precedent cities (NYC) to larger markets
AI disintermediation: third-party AI travel agents winning the interface layer before Airbnb's own 2027 launch
Services/Experiences investment failing to scale into a durable, profitable revenue line

Estimate risk: the FY2026 working-capital unwind (-$350M bridge item) and the float-income exclusion are judgments, not filing figures; Q4/FY2027 guidance from the Q3 call was not available to this build

unchanged_assumptions.left_alone: Growth years 2-10 (all scenarios); EBITDA margin years 3-10 base, 2-10 bull, 5-10 bear; SBC terminal levels (10% / 8% / 13%) and the bear SBC path beyond year 1; cash-tax paths; WACC 9% / 8% / 11%; terminal growth 3.0 / 3.5 / 2.0; terminal caps 20x / 20x / 15x; weights 15/50/35; hurdle 15%; flat 597M share count.
unchanged_assumptions.what_would_move_them: Q4/FY2027 guidance (growth years 2-3); a full year of SBC-incl-award-taxes below 17% of revenue or an explicit management SBC target (SBC glide, either direction); deferred tax assets running off faster than ~$330M/yr (cash-tax ramp); a second major-market STR ban or a take-rate cut (bear weight); RNPL adoption stabilising with unearned fees growing again (wc_capture back above 0); the per-scenario WACC spread is a prior judgment kept for comparability -- the house rule of charging risk once would argue for a single 9%.
